concepts.why: The patient has a positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status.
The patient presents with violaceous discoloration, longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate, which are characteristic of nail lichen planus.
The patient has lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa, which is a characteristic feature of oral lichen planus.
The patient presents with features of both nail and oral lichen planus, suggesting a diagnosis of lichen planus.
The patient presents with painful swelling of the proximal nail folds, dripping of blood from the fingernails and toenails, and occasional pus discharge, which are characteristic of paronychia.
The patient has a positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and presents with features of lichen planus, suggesting a diagnosis of hepatitis C virus-associated lichen planus.
The patient presents with longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate, which are characteristic of nail dystrophy.
The patient presents with features of both oral and nail lichen planus, suggesting a diagnosis of mucocutaneous lichen planus.
It explains the histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, basal cell degeneration, and dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis.
